newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes fall with NYMEX, ANS deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes fall with NYMEX, ANS deal.

text.p: Spot prices for U.S. West Coast crude fell Friday, under pressure from weaker energy futures and falling discounts in the regional market.
Discounts for local benchmark crude Alaska North Slope (ANS) grew Friday following the sale of full cargo from BP to a Hawaii refinery.
The cargo sold at $1.05 under West Texas Intermediate, a three cent increase from the last discount, done March 31.
"It's going to get wider," the buyer said, noting the possibility of more South American imports, as U.S. Gulf markets deal with staggering numbers of imports.

Crude oil on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) has weakened to its lowest point in over a year this week, as a flotilla of imports from North Sea and West African was offered for sale in the U.S. Gulf.
May deliveries of West Texas Intermediate crude fell 35 cents to $19.12 a barrel Friday.
The outright price for ANS slipped 33 cents from Thursday to $18.00/18.00 a barrel in line with NYMEX crude markets.
California heavy grades also fell Friday, after Chevron and Mobil lowered their average posted price 75 cents.
The grade has fallen over $4 since January and continues to come under pressure from a weaker WTI, traders said.
